\(\vec{u}\times\vec{v}=\big(1\cdot(-2)-(-2)\cdot2\big)\hat{i}-\big(2\cdot(-2)-(-2)\cdot1\big)\hat{j}+\big(2\cdot2-1\cdot1\big)\hat{k}\)
\(=2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\)
\(|\vec{u}\times\vec{v}|=\sqrt{2^2+2^2+3^2}=\sqrt{17}\)
Since \(\vec{u}\times\vec{v}\) is perpendicular to both \(\vec{u}\) and \(\vec{v}\), the required unit vectors are
\(\pm\dfrac{2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}}{\sqrt{17}}\).

Direction cosines satisfy \(\cos^2\alpha+\cos^2\beta+\cos^2\gamma=1\).
With \(\alpha=45^\circ,\ \beta=60^\circ\):
\(\cos^2 45^\circ+\cos^2 60^\circ+\cos^2\gamma=1\)
\(\dfrac12+\dfrac14+\cos^2\gamma=1\ \Rightarrow\ \cos^2\gamma=\dfrac14\ \Rightarrow\ \cos\gamma=\pm\dfrac12\)
So the third direction angle is \(\gamma=60^\circ\) or \(\gamma=120^\circ\).

Direction cosines of a line making angles \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) with the axes are \(l=\cos\alpha,\ m=\cos\beta,\ n=\cos\gamma\).
\(l=\cos90^\circ=0,\quad m=\cos135^\circ=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2},\quad n=\cos45^\circ=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\)
Check: \(l^2+m^2+n^2=0+\dfrac12+\dfrac12=1\), as required.
Direction cosines: \(\left(0,\,-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2},\,\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\right)\).

Direction ratios: \(4,-12,18\).
Magnitude \(=\sqrt{4^2+(-12)^2+18^2}=\sqrt{16+144+324}=\sqrt{484}=22\)
Direction cosines \(=\left(\dfrac{4}{22},\dfrac{-12}{22},\dfrac{18}{22}\right)=\left(\dfrac{2}{11},-\dfrac{6}{11},\dfrac{9}{11}\right)\).

Direction ratios of \(\vec{AB}\) are \(-2,2,1\).
Magnitude of \((-2,2,1)=\sqrt{4+4+1}=3\)
Direction cosines \(=\left(-\dfrac23,\dfrac23,\dfrac13\right)\)
Since \(l(AB)=6\), \(B=A+6(l,m,n)=(4,1,5)+6\left(-\dfrac23,\dfrac23,\dfrac13\right)=(4-4,\ 1+4,\ 5+2)\)
\(B=(0,5,7)\).

From \(5l+m+3n=0\), \(m=-5l-3n\).
Substitute in \(5mn-2nl+6lm=0\):
\(5(-5l-3n)n-2nl+6l(-5l-3n)=0\)
\(-25ln-15n^2-2nl-30l^2-18ln=0\)
\(-30l^2-45ln-15n^2=0\ \Rightarrow\ 2l^2+3ln+n^2=0\ \Rightarrow\ (2l+n)(l+n)=0\)
Case 1: \(n=-2l\Rightarrow m=-5l-3(-2l)=l\), direction ratios \((1,1,-2)\).
Case 2: \(n=-l\Rightarrow m=-5l-3(-l)=-2l\), direction ratios \((1,-2,-1)\).
\(\cos\theta=\dfrac{(1)(1)+(1)(-2)+(-2)(-1)}{\sqrt{1+1+4}\,\sqrt{1+4+1}}=\dfrac{1}{6}\)
Angle \(\theta=\cos^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac16\right)\).

Given \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=0\) (perpendicular).
\((\vec{a}+\vec{b})^2=|\vec{a}|^2+2\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}+|\vec{b}|^2=|\vec{a}|^2+|\vec{b}|^2\)
\((\vec{a}-\vec{b})^2=|\vec{a}|^2-2\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}+|\vec{b}|^2=|\vec{a}|^2+|\vec{b}|^2\)
Since both equal \(|\vec{a}|^2+|\vec{b}|^2\), \((\vec{a}+\vec{b})^2=(\vec{a}-\vec{b})^2\). Hence proved.

Let \(\vec{m}=xc\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\), \(\vec{n}=x\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2cx\hat{k}\).
\(\vec{m}\cdot\vec{n}=cx^2-12+6cx=cx^2+6cx-12\)
For an obtuse angle we need \(\vec{m}\cdot\vec{n}<0\) for every real \(x\).
Treating \(f(x)=cx^2+6cx-12\) as a quadratic in \(x\), for \(f(x)<0\) for all \(x\) we need \(c<0\) (downward-opening parabola) and discriminant \(<0\):
\((6c)^2-4c(-12)<0\ \Rightarrow\ 36c^2+48c<0\ \Rightarrow\ 12c(3c+4)<0\ \Rightarrow\ -\dfrac43<c<0\)
Hence \(c\in\left(-\dfrac43,\,0\right)\).

The vector is \(\vec{v}=p\hat{i}+q\hat{j}+r\hat{k}\) with \(p=2,q=3,r=4\).
The projection of \(\vec{v}\) on the X, Y and Z axes are its components \(p,q,r\) respectively (since \(\hat{i},\hat{j},\hat{k}\) are unit vectors along the axes).
Sum of lengths of the projections \(=|p|+|q|+|r|=2+3+4=9\).
Hence proved.

Let the quadrilateral have adjacent sides represented by vectors \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\). Since all sides are equal in length and opposite sides are parallel, it is a rhombus, so \(|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|\).
The diagonals are \(\vec{p}=\vec{a}+\vec{b}\) and \(\vec{q}=\vec{a}-\vec{b}\).
\(\vec{p}\cdot\vec{q}=(\vec{a}+\vec{b})\cdot(\vec{a}-\vec{b})=|\vec{a}|^2-|\vec{b}|^2=0\) (since \(|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|\))
Since \(\vec{p}\cdot\vec{q}=0\), the diagonals are perpendicular. Hence proved.

\(\vec{a}=-9\hat{i}+6\hat{j}+15\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b}=6\hat{i}-4\hat{j}-10\hat{k}\)
Compare ratios of corresponding components: \(\dfrac{6}{-9}=\dfrac{-4}{6}=\dfrac{-10}{15}=-\dfrac23\)
Since all ratios are equal, \(\vec{b}=-\dfrac23\vec{a}\); the vectors are scalar multiples of each other.
Hence \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) are parallel (anti-parallel, since the scalar multiple is negative).

\(\vec{a}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b}=5\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\)
\(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=2(5)+3(-2)+(-1)(4)=10-6-4=0\)
Since \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=0\), the vectors \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) are orthogonal.

\(\vec{a}=-\dfrac35\hat{i}+\dfrac12\hat{j}+\dfrac13\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b}=5\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\)
\(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=\left(-\dfrac35\right)(5)+\left(\dfrac12\right)(4)+\left(\dfrac13\right)(3)=-3+2+1=0\)
Since \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=0\), the vectors \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) are orthogonal.

\(\vec{a}=4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+6\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b}=5\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\)
\(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=4(5)+(-1)(-2)+6(4)=20+2+24=46\neq0\), so the vectors are not orthogonal.
Ratios of components: \(\dfrac{4}{5},\ \dfrac{-1}{-2}=\dfrac12,\ \dfrac{6}{4}=\dfrac32\) — not all equal, so the vectors are not parallel.
Hence \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) are neither orthogonal nor parallel.

Since \(\hat{p}+\hat{r}=\hat{q}\) with \(|\hat{p}|=|\hat{q}|=|\hat{r}|=1\):
\(|\hat{q}|^2=|\hat{p}+\hat{r}|^2=|\hat{p}|^2+2\hat{p}\cdot\hat{r}+|\hat{r}|^2\)
\(1=1+2\hat{p}\cdot\hat{r}+1\ \Rightarrow\ \hat{p}\cdot\hat{r}=-\dfrac12\)
Now \(\hat{p}\cdot\hat{q}=\hat{p}\cdot(\hat{p}+\hat{r})=|\hat{p}|^2+\hat{p}\cdot\hat{r}=1-\dfrac12=\dfrac12\)
\(\hat{p}\cdot\hat{q}=\dfrac12\).

Since \(\hat{p}+\hat{r}=\hat{q}\) with \(|\hat{p}|=|\hat{q}|=|\hat{r}|=1\):
\(|\hat{q}|^2=|\hat{p}+\hat{r}|^2=|\hat{p}|^2+2\hat{p}\cdot\hat{r}+|\hat{r}|^2\)
\(1=1+2\hat{p}\cdot\hat{r}+1\)
\(\hat{p}\cdot\hat{r}=-\dfrac12\).

Let \(O\) be the centre of the circle, radius \(r\), taken as the origin. Let the diameter be \(AB\) with position vectors \(\vec{a}\) and \(-\vec{a}\) (so \(|\vec{a}|=r\)), and let \(P\) be any point on the semicircle with position vector \(\vec{p}\), \(|\vec{p}|=r\).
\(\vec{PA}=\vec{a}-\vec{p},\quad \vec{PB}=-\vec{a}-\vec{p}\)
\(\vec{PA}\cdot\vec{PB}=(\vec{a}-\vec{p})\cdot(-\vec{a}-\vec{p})=-(\vec{a}-\vec{p})\cdot(\vec{a}+\vec{p})=-(|\vec{a}|^2-|\vec{p}|^2)=-(r^2-r^2)=0\)
Since \(\vec{PA}\cdot\vec{PB}=0\), \(\vec{PA}\perp\vec{PB}\), i.e. \(\angle APB=90^\circ\). Hence the angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circle is a right angle.

Let \(\vec{r}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}\).
\(\vec{r}\cdot(3\hat{i}-5\hat{k})=-1\ \Rightarrow\ 3x-5z=-1\) ...(1)
\(\vec{r}\cdot(2\hat{i}+7\hat{j})=6\ \Rightarrow\ 2x+7y=6\) ...(2)
\(\vec{r}\cdot(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})=5\ \Rightarrow\ x+y+z=5\) ...(3)
From (3): \(z=5-x-y\). Substituting in (1): \(3x-5(5-x-y)=-1\ \Rightarrow\ 8x+5y=24\) ...(4)
From (2): \(x=\dfrac{6-7y}{2}\). Substituting in (4): \(4(6-7y)+5y=24\ \Rightarrow\ 24-23y=24\ \Rightarrow\ y=0\)
Then \(x=3\), and \(z=5-3-0=2\).
\(\vec{r}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{k}\).

Given \(\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}=\vec{0}\), \(|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|=|\vec{c}|=1\).
\(|\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}|^2=0\)
\(|\vec{a}|^2+|\vec{b}|^2+|\vec{c}|^2+2(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}+\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}+\vec{c}\cdot\vec{a})=0\)
\(3+2(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}+\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}+\vec{c}\cdot\vec{a})=0\)
\(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}+\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}+\vec{c}\cdot\vec{a}=-\dfrac32\).

\(\vec{a}=3\vec{p}-\vec{q}\), \(\vec{b}=\vec{p}+3\vec{q}\), \(|\vec{p}|=|\vec{q}|=2\), angle between \(\vec{p},\vec{q}\) is \(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\).
\(\vec{p}\cdot\vec{q}=|\vec{p}||\vec{q}|\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3}=2\cdot2\cdot\dfrac12=2\)
\(|\vec{a}|^2=|3\vec{p}-\vec{q}|^2=9|\vec{p}|^2-6\vec{p}\cdot\vec{q}+|\vec{q}|^2=9(4)-6(2)+4=28\)
\(|\vec{b}|^2=|\vec{p}+3\vec{q}|^2=|\vec{p}|^2+6\vec{p}\cdot\vec{q}+9|\vec{q}|^2=4+12+36=52\)
\(|\vec{a}|=2\sqrt7,\quad |\vec{b}|=2\sqrt{13}\)
\(|\vec{a}|:|\vec{b}|=2\sqrt7:2\sqrt{13}=\sqrt7:\sqrt{13}\). Hence proved.

\(\vec{a}=5\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b}=3\hat{i}+\hat{k}\)
Component of \(\vec{a}\) parallel to \(\vec{b}\): \(\vec{a}_{\parallel}=\dfrac{\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}}{|\vec{b}|^2}\vec{b}\)
\(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=15+0+5=20,\quad |\vec{b}|^2=9+0+1=10\)
\(\vec{a}_{\parallel}=\dfrac{20}{10}\vec{b}=2(3\hat{i}+\hat{k})=6\hat{i}+2\hat{k}\)
Perpendicular component: \(\vec{a}_{\perp}=\vec{a}-\vec{a}_{\parallel}=(5-6)\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+(5-2)\hat{k}=-\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\)
Check: \(\vec{a}_{\perp}\cdot\vec{b}=-3+0+3=0\), confirming perpendicularity.
\(\vec{a}=(6\hat{i}+2\hat{k})+(-\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})\), the first part parallel to \(\vec{b}\) and the second perpendicular to \(\vec{b}\).

\(|\vec{u}|=\sqrt{4+1+4}=3,\ |\vec{v}|=\sqrt{1+4+4}=3,\ |\vec{w}|=\sqrt{4+4+1}=3\) — all equal magnitude 3.
Let \(\vec{n}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}\) be a unit vector making equal angles with \(\vec{u},\vec{v},\vec{w}\). Since the magnitudes are equal, this requires \(\vec{n}\cdot\vec{u}=\vec{n}\cdot\vec{v}=\vec{n}\cdot\vec{w}\).
\(\vec{n}\cdot\vec{u}=2x+y-2z,\quad \vec{n}\cdot\vec{v}=x+2y-2z,\quad \vec{n}\cdot\vec{w}=2x-2y+z\)
Setting \(\vec{n}\cdot\vec{u}=\vec{n}\cdot\vec{v}\): \(2x+y=x+2y\Rightarrow x=y\)
Setting \(\vec{n}\cdot\vec{v}=\vec{n}\cdot\vec{w}\): \(-x+4y-3z=0\); with \(x=y\), this gives \(y=z\)
So \(x=y=z\). Since \(\vec{n}\) is a unit vector: \(3x^2=1\Rightarrow x=\pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\)
Required unit vectors: \(\pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})\).

\(y=x^2\) and \(y=x^3\) intersect where \(x^2=x^3\Rightarrow x^2(x-1)=0\Rightarrow x=0,1\), giving points \((0,0)\) and \((1,1)\).
Slopes: for \(y=x^2\), \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2x\); for \(y=x^3\), \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3x^2\).
At \((1,1)\): \(m_1=2,\ m_2=3\)
\(\tan\theta=\left|\dfrac{m_1-m_2}{1+m_1m_2}\right|=\left|\dfrac{2-3}{1+6}\right|=\dfrac17\)
\(\theta=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac17\right)\)
At \((0,0)\): \(m_1=m_2=0\), so both curves share the same tangent line (the X-axis) there; the angle between them at the origin is \(0^\circ\).

\(\vec{v}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\)
Magnitude \(=\sqrt{4+1+4}=3\)
Direction cosines: \(l=\dfrac23,\ m=\dfrac13,\ n=\dfrac23\)
Direction angles: \(\alpha=\cos^{-1}\dfrac23,\ \beta=\cos^{-1}\dfrac13,\ \gamma=\cos^{-1}\dfrac23\).

\(\vec{v}=\dfrac12\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\)
Magnitude \(=\sqrt{\dfrac14+1+1}=\sqrt{\dfrac94}=\dfrac32\)
Direction cosines: \(l=\dfrac{1/2}{3/2}=\dfrac13,\ m=\dfrac{1}{3/2}=\dfrac23,\ n=\dfrac{1}{3/2}=\dfrac23\)
Direction angles: \(\alpha=\cos^{-1}\dfrac13,\ \beta=\cos^{-1}\dfrac23,\ \gamma=\cos^{-1}\dfrac23\).

\(\vec{b}=4\hat{i}+3\hat{j}\), \(|\vec{b}|=5\), so \(\hat{b}=\dfrac45\hat{i}+\dfrac35\hat{j}\).
Since \(\vec{c}\) is perpendicular to \(\vec{b}\) and lies in the XY-plane, take \(\hat{c}=-\dfrac35\hat{i}+\dfrac45\hat{j}\).
The required vector has projections \(1\) along \(\hat{b}\) and \(2\) along \(\hat{c}\):
\(\vec{r}=1\cdot\hat{b}+2\cdot\hat{c}=\left(\dfrac45-\dfrac65\right)\hat{i}+\left(\dfrac35+\dfrac85\right)\hat{j}\)
\(\vec{r}=-\dfrac25\hat{i}+\dfrac{11}{5}\hat{j}\).

If such a line existed, its direction cosines would satisfy \(\cos^2\dfrac{\pi}{6}+\cos^2\dfrac{\pi}{4}+\cos^2\gamma=1\).
\(\cos^2\dfrac{\pi}{6}=\dfrac34,\quad \cos^2\dfrac{\pi}{4}=\dfrac12\)
\(\dfrac34+\dfrac12+\cos^2\gamma=1\ \Rightarrow\ \cos^2\gamma=1-\dfrac54=-\dfrac14\)
Since \(\cos^2\gamma\) cannot be negative, no such \(\gamma\) exists. Hence no line in space can make angles \(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\) and \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\) with the X and Y axes respectively.

From \(3l+m+5n=0\), \(m=-3l-5n\).
Substitute in \(6mn-2nl+5lm=0\):
\(6(-3l-5n)n-2nl+5l(-3l-5n)=0\)
\(-18ln-30n^2-2nl-15l^2-25ln=0\)
\(-15l^2-45ln-30n^2=0\ \Rightarrow\ l^2+3ln+2n^2=0\ \Rightarrow\ (l+n)(l+2n)=0\)
Case 1: \(l=-n\Rightarrow m=-3(-n)-5n=-2n\), direction ratios \((1,2,-1)\).
Case 2: \(l=-2n\Rightarrow m=-3(-2n)-5n=n\), direction ratios \((-2,1,1)\).
\(\cos\theta=\dfrac{(1)(-2)+(2)(1)+(-1)(1)}{\sqrt{1+4+1}\sqrt{4+1+1}}=\dfrac{-1}{6}\)
Taking the acute angle between the lines, \(\theta=\cos^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac16\right)\).

No, \(\vec{b}=\vec{c}\) does not necessarily follow.
\(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}\ \Rightarrow\ \vec{a}\cdot(\vec{b}-\vec{c})=0\), which only means \(\vec{b}-\vec{c}\) is perpendicular to \(\vec{a}\) (or is the zero vector); it need not be zero itself.
Counter-example: let \(\vec{a}=\hat{i}\), \(\vec{b}=\hat{j}\), \(\vec{c}=\hat{k}\). Then \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=0=\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}\), but \(\vec{b}\neq\vec{c}\).

Let the tetrahedron be \(ABCD\) and take \(A\) as the origin, with position vectors \(\vec{b}=\vec{AB},\ \vec{c}=\vec{AC},\ \vec{d}=\vec{AD}\).
Then \(\vec{CD}=\vec{d}-\vec{c},\ \vec{BD}=\vec{d}-\vec{b},\ \vec{BC}=\vec{c}-\vec{b}\).
Given \(AB\perp CD\): \(\vec{b}\cdot(\vec{d}-\vec{c})=0\ \Rightarrow\ \vec{b}\cdot\vec{d}=\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}\) ...(1)
Given \(AC\perp BD\): \(\vec{c}\cdot(\vec{d}-\vec{b})=0\ \Rightarrow\ \vec{c}\cdot\vec{d}=\vec{c}\cdot\vec{b}\) ...(2)
From (1) and (2): \(\vec{b}\cdot\vec{d}=\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}=\vec{c}\cdot\vec{d}\)
Now \(\vec{AD}\cdot\vec{BC}=\vec{d}\cdot(\vec{c}-\vec{b})=\vec{d}\cdot\vec{c}-\vec{d}\cdot\vec{b}=\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}-\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}=0\) (using (1) and (2))
Hence \(AD\perp BC\); the third pair of opposite edges is also perpendicular. Hence proved.

\(|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|=1,\ \vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=0,\ \vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}=\vec{0}\Rightarrow\vec{c}=-(\vec{a}+\vec{b})\)
\(|\vec{c}|^2=|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|^2=|\vec{a}|^2+2\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}+|\vec{b}|^2=1+0+1=2\)
\(|\vec{c}|=\sqrt2\).

\(\vec{a}\) lies in the YZ-plane, so its \(\hat{i}\)-component is \(0\).
It makes \(60^\circ\) with the positive Y-axis, so the \(\hat{j}\)-component \(=|\vec{a}|\cos60^\circ=4\cdot\dfrac12=2\)
Since \(|\vec{a}|=4\): \(y^2+z^2=16\Rightarrow z^2=16-4=12\Rightarrow z=\pm2\sqrt3\)
\(\vec{a}=2\hat{j}\pm2\sqrt3\hat{k}\).

\(\vec{a}\) lies in the XZ-plane, so its \(\hat{j}\)-component is \(0\).
It makes \(45^\circ\) with the positive Z-axis, so the \(\hat{k}\)-component \(=|\vec{a}|\cos45^\circ=10\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}=5\sqrt2\)
Since \(|\vec{a}|=10\): \(x^2+z^2=100\Rightarrow x^2=100-50=50\Rightarrow x=\pm5\sqrt2\)
\(\vec{a}=\pm5\sqrt2\hat{i}+5\sqrt2\hat{k}\).
